changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Email the client a PDF of their signed SA as soon as they sign, copied to whoever the SA was copied to

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let the client download their signed SA from the completion screen and every time they open the link again

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Download the signed SA as a PDF from Client Confirmation, and list every SA version on the load with its own PDF

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Keep every SA review round as a verification record, with who ticked what and the facts when it was sent, opened from Client Confirmation

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Retire Carrier Assigned as a step: after Booked comes Client Signed, by the client's signature or by hand

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let a task be picked as planning time, including one already done today or with no set time
changes.body:
The "Use one you have" list now offers tasks with a day but no time, and a
one-off task already ticked done today, which already counted as covering
the slot. The Calendar's Planning time card gets its own "Use one you have"
link that opens the list directly.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Remind people to clock in at the start of their shift, and not on weekends, holidays or days off

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let dispatch copy the SA to extra addresses, and check carrier age, the driver's license, truck pictures and accessorials before it goes out

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Send the SA with the quote PDF and a QR code, keep one signing link per load that updates when the order changes, and let dispatch edit the agreement terms
changes.body:
- The client's SA email attaches the quote PDF and shows a QR code; the QR on the PDF is clickable.
- The signing page shows every stop with its address and dates, the freight, the client's payment terms and the terms and conditions, and records name, title, e-sign consent and acceptance of the terms.
- Agreement Terms panel in Settings > Operations under the new agreementTerms.manage permission (admin and dispatch). Each link keeps the terms it was sent with.
- One link per load: sending again with nothing changed re-emails the same link. A saved change holds the link, reopens the SA request for dispatch and admins, and clears a client signature that no longer matches. Sending after review revises the same link and QR in place, keeping every earlier version and signature.
- The order shows the signing link to copy, and a staff-only preview that cannot be signed.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Show links in chat alerts in full, clickable, with a Copy link button

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Draw the chat alerts menu over the page so the sidebar cannot cut it off

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Send Back on a carrier opened from an order to that order, not the carriers list

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Send Back on a shipper or consignee to the list it was opened from, not Clients

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Send Back on a client, shipper or consignee opened from an order to that order, not the clients list

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Replace "Booked" with Request SA, and give admin and dispatch a review-and-send flow for the Shipper Agreement
changes.body:
A quote's next step is now Request SA: it records a request
(saRequests/{orderId}), moves the order to booked, adds admin and dispatch
to the load's discussion room and posts there, which puts it in their chat
inbox with a notification. On the order they see what TTMS checked (SA and
BOL fields, insurance date, FMCSA concerns, a carrier phone that differs
from FMCSA's) beside a double-check list they tick, each tick named. Send
SA is unlocked by the list, emails the client and posts the e-signature
link in the room; Mark done closes it and names who did. Requests can be
sent back to the broker with a reason. Approvals lists them all.

The e-signature now also records the signer's device (user agent and a
readable summary) beside name, IP and time.

firestore.rules changes (saRequests closed): not live until deployed.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add a quote PDF and a paperwork checklist to orders in the quote phase
changes.body:
While an order is a quote, the broker can download a client-facing quote
PDF built from the order as it stands: lane, dates, freight, price, and a
"to confirm this load we still need" list. Beside it, a checklist shows
what the Shipper Agreement and the BOL still need, from one definition
(src/types/orderReadiness.ts) that dispatch's SA review will share.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let any other file be attached to an order, from its Documents tab
changes.body:
Receipts, scale tickets, customs papers, permits, emails: any number of
files of any type, up to 25 MB each, with a kind and a note. Uploaded into
a create-only order-files/ prefix, then checked and recorded by
POST /api/orders/{id}/files; read only through signed links after the
same canSeeOrder() check. Adding and removing write the change log.

storage.rules and firestore.rules change: not live until deployed.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add a quote calculator, on its own page and from Price and Terms on the order form, with an admin-editable rate card
changes.body:
Distance from two ZIP codes or typed in miles, km or meters; freight in any
unit with a fit check against every truck; price from the rate card at a
low-to-high point; driver pay, broker fee and margin, a uShip column, a
check of driver pay against DAT's weekly national averages, and copy-out
text with or without costs. "Apply to order" fills Agreed Rate and Broker Fee.

Rates start from the old Google Sheet and live in appSettings/quoteRates,
edited in Settings > Operations > Quote Rates under the new
quoteRates.manage permission (admin only by default).

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let each freight line say which pickup and delivery it goes through, and record vehicle details per line, both shown on the BOL
changes.body:
On a load with more than one pickup or delivery, every commodity line can
name its stops ("Picked up at" / "Delivered to"). The BOL gets a column for
it and lists what is loaded or unloaded at each stop; the order page shows it
under each line. Removing a stop renumbers the lines that pointed past it.

Freight lines can also carry year, make, model, colour, VIN, type and
condition when the freight is a vehicle.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Count steps as well as tasks in each board column's badge

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add break, lunch and active pause reminders, with a daily set of exercises in English and Spanish
changes.body:
A reminder at 10am to take the 20-minute break by 11, and at 1pm for lunch
(1 to 2), Monday to Friday, for anybody clocked in and not already on a
break. A card in the corner of TTMS and a desktop notification; either
starts the break in one click.

An optional active pause once a day (8:30, off until HR turns it on) shows
three short desk exercises, different every day, in English and Spanish.

HR and admins change all three for the company or one person in
Attendance > Setup > Break reminders. Worked out in the browser from the
clock state, so there is no new cron and no extra reads per check.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Make board columns equal height, scroll the page while dragging near its edges, and add a right-click Move to menu on cards and steps

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let a planning slot be any length from the prompt, and keep the Planning time card in step with the calendar

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Keep the calendar's side panels beside it when zoomed in, and widen the page instead
changes.body:
Zooming used to move the Today panel below the grid. Now the page drops its
width cap while zoomed, so the calendar grows into the rest of the screen and
pushes the panels to the right edge.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add Break, Focus time, Training and Planning event types, and drop Appointment
changes.body: An event still stored as an appointment reads as Other event.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let a task or event be duplicated from its editor

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let a step be dragged to its own column on the board, and show that status in every view

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let steps be dragged into a new order, and give the daily planning tasks new starting steps

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let task times be typed, and pick them on slower wheels
changes.body:
The task editor's time boxes were the browser's own, whose drop-down flings
past several rows per mouse-wheel notch and which few people realised could
be typed into. TimeField takes a time written any ordinary way and opens the
planning card's one-row-per-notch wheels from a clock button.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Replace the calendar's Bigger switch with zoom in and zoom out
changes.body:
Four steps, 100% to 250%: taller hours, larger type, and from the second
step up the full width and event names that wrap instead of being cut
off. Month squares grow and show more before "+N more". Zooming keeps the
hour at the top of the window in place. Saved per browser; anyone who had
Bigger on opens at 150%.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Give tasks a start and end time that set their block on the calendar
changes.body:
The due date and time stay the deadline. A task's end can be pulled on the
week grid, and moving or repeating a task keeps its length.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Start new tasks and events in the colours of their calendar switches
changes.body:
A new task starts royal blue and a new event cyan, matching the My tasks
and My events switches on the Calendar, instead of yellow for both. The
editor follows the Task/Event toggle until a colour is picked. Items
already saved keep their colours.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Base a task's XP on its difficulty instead of its priority
changes.body:
Game mode now asks for a difficulty (Trivial, Easy, Medium, Hard, Very hard,
Epic) in the task editor, and that alone sets what a task earns and what it
costs when overdue or not done. Priority no longer touches XP. The
hard-task missions count Hard and above. Tasks saved before this read as
Medium.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let the planning card's hour and minute wheels go round instead of stopping at the end

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let an order have more than one pickup and more than one delivery
changes.body:
The first pickup and delivery stay in their existing fields; further stops
are listed in extraPickups / extraDeliveries beside them, so every existing
order, query, index and import keeps working with no migration. The forms,
order page, BOL, agreement emails, invoice, search, change log, trip distance
and map link all cover every stop. A party's page finds loads it is a later
stop on through stopPartyIds and its new index.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Count deliveries for the week and cut dashboard dates at the user's midnight
changes.body:
The "Delivered today" card is now "Delivered this week": loads whose
delivery date falls between Sunday 00:00 and the next Sunday, whatever
their status now, so a load closed out after delivering still counts.
Old ?view=delivered_today links open the weekly list.

Every date card (today, this week, this month) and the list each one
opens now start at midnight in the browser's time zone, falling back to
Guatemala, instead of the server's UTC clock, which put midnight at 6pm
the evening before.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Show commas in money amount boxes as they are typed

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Keep a change log of every order, client, shipper, consignee and carrier
changes.body:
Every save now records who changed what, from what to what, and when, in a
changes subcollection, shown as a History tab on orders and carriers and a
Change log section on parties. Saves moved from the browser to server routes
so the entry is written in the same batch as the change and cannot be
skipped; firestore.rules now refuses client writes to all three collections.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Show city, state and ZIP in a client's order routes

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Open a carrier by clicking its name

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Open a client, shipper or consignee by clicking its name

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let weekly and monthly planning be set for just this week or month
changes.body:
The planning card's repeat box now shows for every kind. Weekly and
monthly start ticked, as before, but can be unticked to add a one-off;
the card then asks again on the next Friday afternoon or the last Friday
of next month.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Ask before closing a task or event with unsaved changes
changes.body:
Clicking outside the editor, Escape, the X and Cancel now confirm before
throwing away anything typed or picked, for new items and edits alike.
Escape in a board column's quick-add box asks too when it holds text.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let people add their own task colours
changes.body:
Six extra colours (Olive, Lime, Moss, Grape, Orchid, Magenta) can be added
from Edit colours on My tasks, named, and removed again. Each is a hue
picked from the gaps between the six task colours, the calendar layers and
red, and globals.css works out its shades for light, dim and dark the same
way tailwind.config.ts does for a colour family, so none can come out
unreadable. An extra colour exists while it has a name; removing one moves
its tasks to yellow.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Keep calendar layer colours apart from the task colours
changes.body:
Birthdays move from pink to indigo, work anniversaries from brand blue to
teal, US holidays from sky to outlined grey, and the My tasks and My events
switches from yellow and violet to brand. None of them now matches one of
the six colours a task or event can be given.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Give tasks a deadline separate from their planned day
changes.body:
A task's date and time are now when it is planned to be worked on (calendar,
reminders, repeats), and a new optional dueDate/dueTime is its deadline.
Overdue, the queue order, Up next and game-mode lateness go through
deadlineOf(), which falls back to the planned day when there is no deadline,
so tasks saved before this behave as they always did. The editor, table,
board, sticky notes, queue and calendar show both; the calendar marks a
deadline on its own day.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let the planning card rename the slot before adding it
changes.body:
The title in the card's preview is now a text box. What is typed there
is the task's title on the calendar, the board and the reminder; left
blank, the kind's usual name is saved.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Make the planning time picker move one row per wheel notch
changes.body:
A mouse wheel notch scrolled two or three rows of the hour and minute
wheels, so people overshot the time they wanted. The wheel now steps one
row per notch, a trackpad one row per row's height of travel, and arrow
keys and clicks glide to the row instead of jumping.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let the task editor set a planning slot's end time
changes.body:
The Ends box was drawn for events only, so a planning slot (a task that
keeps an end) could only be lengthened by stretching it on the calendar.
The editor now shows Ends for a planning slot, sends it on save, and moves
the end with the start so a changed start keeps the same length.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add day and four-day views, a bigger calendar size, one-click events, and drop previews
changes.body:
Dragging in the hour grid now draws the item where it will land, with its
times, and dims the original. Hovering an empty spot outlines the hour a
click would create, and one click creates it. The calendar gains Day and
4 days views beside Week and Month, and a Bigger size with taller hours and
the full width, both remembered per browser.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let the planning card use a task or event you already have
changes.body:
"Use one you have" on the planning card lists your own upcoming timed
tasks and events and links the one you pick as that planning time,
instead of making a new slot. Nothing is recognised by its title. A
repeat past its end no longer counts as on the calendar, so the card
asks again.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let planning prompts take any time, keep weekly and monthly to their Friday afternoon, and pick the monthly day

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Move old tasks into a history store and give every repeat an end date
changes.body:
History: anything finished or past more than 90 days ago moves out of the task
list once a day, so opening My tasks or the Calendar reads only recent and open
work. Open tasks and repeating series never move. The Calendar fetches history
a month at a time only when paged back that far, and shows it read-only.

Repeat ends: every repeating task and event now stops on a date the person
picks, a month by default. Setting it longer shows a warning that advises
against it. Repeating planning slots also end after a month, and the planning
card asks again when they do.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add planning prompts, repeating events, an hour grid and task outcomes to the calendar
changes.body:
Planning prompts: a card that asks for a time for a morning review, end-of-day
planning for tomorrow, weekly planning on Friday and monthly planning on the
last Friday, and adds it as a task with a reminder. The daily ones are one-off
unless "every weekday" is ticked. The card shows the day it lands on within the
person's working hours (7am to 4pm when HR has set none) and can move things
out of the way.

Repeats: "every month by weekday" (1st Tuesday, 2nd and 4th Wednesday, last
Friday), and events can now repeat as a series. One date of a series can be
dragged or stretched on its own, after asking, and becomes a separate event.

Calendar: the week view is an hour grid on desktop. Drag blocks to another day
or time, pull an event's bottom edge to change its length, double-click to add.

Tasks: a closed task records Done, Not done or Rescheduled and stays on its
day. Not done costs XP in game mode and is refunded if undone. Reschedule
keeps the original on its day and carries a copy forward. "Clear done" takes
finished tasks off My tasks but keeps them on the calendar.

Attendance: the "Standard week" button fills in 7am to 4pm.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Find carrier insurers FMCSA left in its pre-Motus file, and fill in the DOT
changes.body:
The insurer and policy came only from FMCSA's new Motus file, which is
missing most filings made before the May 2026 switch (about 132,000 against
468,000 in the old active/pending file). The old file is now read too, by the
DOT padded to eight digits, and its filings count only when Motus has nothing
newer of that kind, has not cancelled it since, and FMCSA's live answer still
shows insurance of that kind on file.

The census lookup (phone, email) took 9 to 43 seconds and timed out at 10,
taking the insurance results with it. It now gets 30 seconds, fails on its
own, and both it and the other open-data queries wait and retry when told
"too many requests". The bulk check runs two carriers at a time.

The carrier page's "Fill in from FMCSA" now offers the DOT under the same
guard the bulk check uses, then checks again by it.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Check imported carriers with FMCSA and fill in their blank details
changes.body:
After a carriers file is imported in Settings -> Data, TTMS now checks each
new or changed carrier with FMCSA in batches, stores the answer, and fills in
only the fields that are blank: DOT (when FMCSA lists our MC under it), phone,
email, address, insurer, policy number and coverage amounts. A "Check carriers
not yet checked" button covers carriers added before this and retries any
FMCSA did not answer for.

The blank-fill rule moves into src/types/fmcsa.ts so the carrier page and the
bulk check share one definition. FMCSA blocks non-US connections with a bare
403; that now reads as a blocked connection rather than a bad key.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Fill carrier phone, email and insurance from FMCSA's registration data
changes.body:
The FMCSA check now also reads FMCSA's daily open data (the Motus datasets
on data.transportation.gov): registered phone, email and officer, the
insurance policies on file, cargo types, pending cancellations and
suspension notices. Adding a carrier fills in phone, email and insurer
from it, and an existing carrier can fill its blank fields with one click.
New warnings for insurance being cancelled with no replacement and for
suspension notices.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add a carrier straight from an FMCSA lookup
changes.body:
Both Add Carrier forms start with a DOT or MC lookup that fills in the
legal name, both numbers and the address, and shows FMCSA's warnings before
saving. When the company is already in TTMS under the same DOT or any of its
MCs it offers that record instead of a second copy. The new carrier is saved
with its FMCSA check filed against it.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Keep the order number from overlapping the client when a load has a picture

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Check carriers with FMCSA for authority, insurance on file and safety record
changes.body:
A Check FMCSA box on the carrier page, and on the order screens where it
refreshes a check over a day old by itself. Flags revoked or missing
authority, no liability insurance on file, out-of-service orders, poor
safety ratings, and an MC on our record that FMCSA does not list under the
DOT number. Warns only; nothing blocks booking.

The lookup runs server-side with FMCSA_WEB_KEY and is stored on the carrier
as `fmcsa`, which the rules now refuse from the browser.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Remove the driver licence search from the Documents screen
changes.body:
Licences are now opened from the order they belong to. The company-wide
listing and its route, /api/documents/licenses, are gone, so no listing
reaches past canSeeOrder() any more.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let tasks link to an order by its number
changes.body:
A task can now carry up to three orders. The editor's Order box takes a TTL
number, a #number for a BATS-era load, or the order's link, and looks it up
through the same access-checked route chat's order cards use, so a typo or
someone else's load is refused rather than saved. The number shows as a link
to the order on the board, sticky notes, queue, path and table, and the task
search finds it. A repeating task's next copy starts without the order.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Give every game level its own hand-drawn picture in each theme
changes.body:
The ring with a shared symbol beside the level name is replaced by a line
drawing in the style of the banner art, one per level per theme (180 in
all), chosen to fit each level's name. It also shows, larger, in the level
up and level down pop-up, red on a level down.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let tasks name colleagues from the directory, with a contact card
changes.body:
A task can now carry up to five people from the directory. They show as
"with @Name" on the board, queue and path, in the bottom-left corner of a
sticky note, and in a With column on the table. Clicking a name opens their
email, work phone, extension, a Message button and their directory page.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Use a clearer flower for the Fairy world's Done column

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Make the Pirates theme titles larger and stop faking bold on them
changes.body:
Pirata One has a single weight, so the bold the titles ask for was being
synthesized by the browser over an already heavy blackletter.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Draw the streak flame in fire colours under every theme

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Make the streak flame flicker while the streak is alive
changes.body:
The flame on the streak card sways from its base with a pulsing glow in
its own colour, in plain mode and every game theme. A dead streak's grey
flame stays still, and the animation is off for anyone who asks their
system for less motion.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Warn when a step is due after its task
changes.body:
The step list in the editor and focus screen flags a step whose due date
falls after the task's own, with a line saying which dates clash. It warns
rather than refuses, since the task's date may be about to move.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Give the game's streak its own card and rename two freight theme labels
changes.body:
The streak was a small figure on the game banner and easy to miss. It now
has the same card beside Up next that the plain streak has, showing the
game's own count in the theme's accent. On the freight theme the banner
reads "Logistics strategy" and the queue "Logistics plans".

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let a task's steps carry due dates of their own
changes.body:
Each step can be given a date from the step list in the editor and focus
screen, and shows when it is due on the board, sticky notes, table, path
and up-next card. A step's date is a label: no reminder, no XP, and it
never makes the task overdue. A repeating task's next copy moves each step
date by as much as the task's own moved.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Show a task's steps as their own cards, notes and table rows
changes.body:
On the board each step is a small card hung under its task in the task's
colour, joined to it by a line and tickable in place. On the sticky notes
each step is a smaller note on a dashed string under its task's note. In
the table, clicking a row with steps opens them underneath as rows of
their own. Steps move with their task and fold away once it is done.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Give the XP badge its own icon in each game theme
changes.body:
It always drew Sparkles, the wizarding theme's Done icon, so under every
theme it read as "done". Each theme now has a reward icon of its own that
repeats no column icon: fuel, a bolt, a medal, a sparkle, a star, coins.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add a Path view that draws the task queue as a road with each task's steps in order

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add an up-next card, a numbered queue, task steps, focus mode and a streak without game mode
changes.body:
The task with the closest deadline is highlighted at the top of My tasks
with a Done button that walks through its steps. Tasks can have steps,
named after the game theme, and a priority number in a new Queue view.
Focus mode shrinks the page to one task. A plain streak runs with game
mode off.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Give sticky notes a status dot and let them size to their text
changes.body:
Each note shows the status ring its board column wears before the title,
and is as tall as what is written on it instead of a fixed square; long
notes stop at 18 lines.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Turn task colours into named tags with a filter bar on My tasks
changes.body:
A bar above the list shows All and each colour with its count; a click
filters every view to that colour, and a new task starts in it while it
is picked. "Name colours" lets each person name the six colours, stored
on personalTasks/{uid}.colorLabels through PUT /api/me/tasks/labels and
shown in the task editor too.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Show the XP a task will earn on its card in game mode
changes.body:
Board cards, sticky notes and table rows show "+30 XP" while a task is
open, discounted when it is late, and what it earned once done. The
figure comes from a new taskXp(), which onTaskDone() now pays from too,
so the number on a card is the number that lands.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Make the Fairy worlds page and column titles bigger
changes.body:
Fairy's script italic reads at half the height of the other display faces,
so a theme can now set its own title sizes. Only Fairy does: column titles
go from 14px to 20px and the page title from 24px to about 34px.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Restore light headings in the dim and dark game-themed My tasks
changes.body:
The light room set the two top inks on the same element and the dim and
dark rooms did not restate them, so column titles and the page heading
kept the light room's deep ink on a dark ground. Every room now names the
same variables.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Colour the task editor with the colour picked for the task
changes.body:
The editor window now wears the same note colours as the board card and
the sticky note, and changes as a colour is clicked, so it previews the
card before saving. Inputs keep their own plain ground.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Make the My tasks game themes follow the light, dim and dark app themes
changes.body:
The themed room used to force the dark palette whatever the app was set
to. It now comes in three versions written as CSS on html.dark and
html.dark.dim: a pale wash of the theme's hue in light, slate in dim, and
the deep room it always had in dark. Pale accents are darkened for words
in the light room, and the banner stays dark in all three.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Colour board cards by the task's colour and make note colours clearer on dark grounds
changes.body:
The board card now takes the colour picked for the task, and its dot shows
the task's status with the same ring as its column header. Under dark mode
and the game theme a note steps up to a stronger tint so the colours stop
reading as mud, and swatches are a solid 400 in every theme.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Lighten the game-themed My tasks page and give it the theme's fonts and icons
changes.body:
The area around the banner is now a few steps lighter than the banner, in
the theme's colour, with brighter grey text to match. Each theme has a
readable body font for the whole page and uses its display font for the page
title and column names. The theme dropdown's options are dark with white
text instead of white on white. Board columns keep their coloured dots and
gain an icon from the chosen theme beside them.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Dress the whole My tasks page in the game theme
changes.body:
With game mode on, the page becomes a dark room in the theme's colours:
columns, task tiles, inputs, the editor and the buttons all follow the
banner, while status colours keep their meaning.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Redesign game themes as a banner with line artwork and one accent
changes.body:
Each theme now has a dark banner with its own drawing, the level, XP and
streak, and a strip with the theme and missions controls. The board takes
a single accent colour instead of a tinted, patterned page.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let the game theme restyle the whole My tasks page
changes.body:
Theme is now its own setting in the game bar. Each theme changes the
page's background, pattern, heading lettering, columns, cards, buttons,
XP bar and a few words, while column names and statuses stay the same.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Count game streaks on weekdays only and freeze them during time off
changes.body:
Weekends, Guatemalan holidays and days covered by the person's own
pending or approved time-off requests no longer break a streak or
charge overdue XP. Weekly attendance missions now count five weekdays.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add repeating tasks and an optional game mode to My tasks
changes.body:
Tasks can repeat every day, weekday, week or month; finishing one adds
the next. Game mode gives private XP, levels with themed titles (freight
by default), a working-day streak, daily and weekly missions, penalties
for overdue tasks, and suggested freight broker tasks.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add Ready and In review columns, and let people arrange their own task board
changes.body:
Columns can be dragged into a new order, hidden, and added. Hiding or
deleting a column moves its tasks back to the nearest showing column on
its left. To do and Done are always shown. The layout is saved per person.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add a change history of every TTMS change for the IT account
changes.body:
A Change history page lists every commit to TTMS, newest first, searchable
by word, by type (New, Change, Fix, Security, Maintenance) and by date
range. Only it@totaltransportlogistics.us can see it: an address test, not
a permission, so it cannot be granted from Settings.

The record is src/lib/data/changelog.json, filled from git by
scripts/update-changelog.js, which now runs before every build. It only
adds, since Vercel clones only the last few commits.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Merge Celebrations into the Calendar and add reminders and event types
changes.body:
One Calendar page for everyone: their own tasks and events plus Guatemala
and US holidays. Admins and HR also get birthdays, anniversaries and the
celebration reminder panels on the same grid, still served only by
/api/celebration-calendar. /dashboard/celebrations now redirects.

Events carry a type (call, online meeting, in-person meeting, company
activity, appointment, other) and a place or meeting link. Tasks and events
can set reminders, sent by email and/or a private "Your reminders" chat
room from a queue (taskReminders) that a five-minute Vercel cron drains.
Dates and times on the calendar are office time.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add a week view and a This week list to My calendar
changes.body:
A Month / Week switch on the calendar. The week view draws every item for
seven days (no "+N more"), takes drops to move a date, and stacks the days
on a phone. Beside the month, a This week list shows the chosen day's week
grouped by day.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add a personal task list and calendar for everyone
changes.body:
My tasks shows each person's own to-dos as a Kanban board (drag between
columns), sticky notes and a sortable table. My calendar shows dated tasks
and appointments by month, and dragging an item to another day changes its
date. Items live at personalTasks/{uid}/items and are read and written only
through /api/me/tasks, so nobody else can see them, admins included.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add a strip of chat pictures to the chat popup for one-click switching
changes.body:
The popup shows one thing at a time, so moving between chats meant going
back to the list every time. An open chat now has the rooms down its left
side, in list order, with the same unread and mention marks. The popup is
widened to 436px so the messages keep their width.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add a search inside a single chat, beside the search of every chat
changes.body:
A magnifier in each chat's header searches only that conversation. On the
full page the results sit in the thread column so the reader can step through
matches while the room scrolls to each; in the popup they replace the room.
The server checks membership before searching the named room, and a room the
caller is not in answers with nothing.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Remember theme, chat wallpaper and Learn English on the account

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Point to new messages below the fold in chat, like WhatsApp
changes.body:
While somebody is scrolled up, a down-arrow button in the corner of the
thread counts the messages that have arrived below them and takes them to
the newest. An @ button beside it counts the ones that name them or quote
them, and each click goes to the next. Counts fall as messages scroll into
view, not all at once at the bottom.

MessageThread is now keyed by conversation in ChatPanel, so the first paint
of a room no longer runs against the previous room's messages.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add load pictures: upload, a sliding reel, a profile picture, and a browser
changes.body:
Brokers can add pictures to a load from its new Pictures tab (file picker,
drag and drop, or the phone camera), tagged with a stage, the commodity line
they show and a caption. They slide left to right in a reel and open in a
full-screen viewer, where one can be made the load's profile picture — shown
beside its number in the order header and the orders list.

The Documents screen gets a Load Pictures view: search, commodity and stage
filters, and six layouts (grid, collage, table, by load, by commodity,
timeline).

Held to the same boundary as the BOL: loadPhotos and load-photos/ are closed
to the browser, and every read and write goes through routes that check
canSeeOrder() first. File paths are derived from ids, never stored. Pictures
are shrunk in the browser to fit Vercel's request limit.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: List carriers' certificates of insurance on the Documents screen
changes.body:
One row per carrier on a load the reader can see, with its insurance status,
expiry and policy, and the reader's own loads on that carrier. A certificate
belongs to the carrier, so the list is carriers rather than loads.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Show Online at once when somebody clocked in comes back to their desk
changes.body:
Idle check-ins while clocked in used the five-minute slot, so somebody who
came back could read as Away in chat for up to five minutes. Now the first
activity after an idle check-in sends a chat-only update straight away -
from a click in TTMS, or from the browser noticing the computer is in use
again. It writes presence only and leaves the slot alone, so the day's
active and idle minutes are still counted once per five minutes.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Count whole-computer activity while clocked in, where the browser allows it
changes.body:
While somebody is clocked in, the heartbeat asks Chrome or Edge (Idle
Detection) whether the computer is in use at all - keyboard, mouse, a
locked screen - so working in another program counts as active. Never
which program or what was typed. Outside clocked-in hours it still counts
TTMS use only. Each day records how it was measured, shown to HR in the
day detail and the CSV, and the staff policy text says so.

At each clock-in until it is allowed, TTMS explains before the browser
asks, or - after a Block, which no site can undo - how to switch it back
on in Site settings. scripts/allow-idle-detection.bat sets the policy on a
PC so nobody is asked; the Google Admin console does not offer it.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Stop chat notifications replaying on every sign-in and reload
changes.body:
The "already seen" map was seeded before the first snapshot arrived, and
the company room and member rooms arrive from separate listeners, so old
messages read as new once the rest loaded. Nothing stamped before the page
started listening is announced now, nor anything already read on any
device, and seeding waits for the conversations to load.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add a Dim colour theme between light and dark
changes.body:
Dark mode felt too heavy for some people. Dim keeps the dark class, so the
light inks and dark browser controls are shared, and adds a dim class that
lifts the grounds to a slate grey. Picked from the sidebar switch, per browser.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add attendance: clock in and out, schedules, time off, and an HR report
changes.body:
Everyone gets a clock in the sidebar (in, out, break, lunch) and a status
colleagues see in chat, plus their own month, time-off and correction
requests and a hide-last-seen option on their profile. HR and admins get
an Attendance page: a month grid with CSV export, request decisions, and
setup for schedules, holiday moves, office networks and alerts. Sales
Managers see their own team. A who's-in-today card sits on the dashboard.

Clock actions record IP, network location, provider (ipinfo), device and
office match. The five-minute heartbeat now goes through the server and
also records active and idle minutes. A nightly job closes forgotten
clock-outs and records absences; a second job posts not-in-yet alerts.
All attendance collections are closed to the browser.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Show online and last seen in one-on-one chats, with a switch for admin and HR
changes.body:
Each browser records a server-stamped time in presence/{uid} at most once
every five minutes while someone is actively using TTMS, shared across tabs
so reloads add nothing. The direct-chat header reads it live and shows
Online or Last seen. Settings > Operations > Online Status turns it off for
everyone, gated on a new presence.manage permission held by admin and HR.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let each person collapse the sidebar, or have it open on hover
changes.body:
Three desktop modes, chosen per browser beside the theme switch: always
open (the default, so nothing changes until somebody asks), folded to a
rail of icons, or a rail that opens over the page under the pointer.
Phones keep the drawer and ignore the setting.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add a Learn English mode with Spanish meanings for work words
changes.body:
A per-browser switch at the foot of the sidebar underlines about 160 words
from a hand-written glossary (screen words, freight terms, office English)
and shows a card with the Spanish, a plain-English meaning, an example and
read-aloud on hover, tap or selection. The underlines use the CSS Custom
Highlight API so the page's DOM is never touched.

My words (/dashboard/words) keeps each person's lookups and "I know this"
marks in vocabulary/{uid}, read and written only through /api/me/words.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Find colleagues you have not chatted with yet from the chat search box

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Ask for the full BATS insurance block when adding a carrier
changes.body:
Both add forms now take insurance company, policy number, expiration,
liability amount and a new cargo amount, plus the certificate. The old
single coverage amount becomes the liability figure; cargo is stored as
insuranceCargoCoverage. The certificate's file name now shows beside
its link.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Ask for notification permission on the first click after sign-in
changes.body:
Desktop chat notifications were already on by default, but did nothing until
somebody found the bell in chat and pressed Allow. Now the browser asks once,
inside the first click anywhere in TTMS, and the bell menu re-reads the
permission each time it opens.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let each person pick a chat background
changes.body:
Six to choose from, in a picker beside the alerts bell: Freight (the
existing one, still the default), Highway, Harbour, Warehouse, Dots and
Plain. Each has its own light and dark colours.

The choice is kept per browser in localStorage, like the colour theme,
so it needs no Firestore read, write or rule. It follows across open
tabs.

scripts/build-chat-wallpaper.mjs now builds one tile per drawn set,
each with its own seed; the Freight tile is byte-for-byte unchanged.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Give chat a WhatsApp-style look with a freight doodle background
changes.body:
Messages now sit on a paper-toned ground with faint freight drawings
(trucks, containers, forklifts, ships, pallets) generated from lucide
icons by scripts/build-chat-wallpaper.mjs and applied as a CSS mask so
dark mode recolours it. Other people's bubbles are white on it.

Start-a-conversation is now a filled round button, and the list header,
room header, search, chips and composer use larger, darker controls.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add a dark mode, switched from the foot of the sidebar
changes.body:
Light, dark, or match the computer, remembered per browser and light by
default. Rather than adding dark: classes to every screen, the Tailwind
config points pale backgrounds, dark text, hairlines and bg-white at CSS
variables that html.dark redefines, so every existing screen follows and
the light theme is unchanged. A script in <head> applies the choice before
the first paint, and native controls and the analytics charts follow too.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let each card on the order page be edited on its own
changes.body:
General, Freight, Price and Terms, Route and Notes each get an Edit button
that opens the edit screen on that section alone and returns to the same
card. A section save writes only that section's fields, so it cannot
overwrite what someone changed elsewhere on the load in the meantime. The
Notes card now always shows so a note can be added from it.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Move Price and Terms between Freight and Route on the order screens
changes.body:
Same position on the order page and the new and edit forms, so all three
read in the same order.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Rename the order Shipment card to General and let pickup and delivery be date ranges
changes.body:
Pieces and weight come off the card since Freight already shows them per
line. Pickup and delivery each gain an optional end date (pickupDateEnd /
deliveryDateEnd); the existing fields stay the first day of the window so
sorting, filters, dashboard counts and alerts are unchanged. The range is
carried onto the agreement emails, signing page, BOL and invoice.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add Klipy GIF search to chat, sharing favorites and folders with stickers
changes.body:
The sticker picker gains a Stickers | GIFs switch. GIFs come from Klipy
through GET /api/chat/gifs, so KLIPY_API_KEY stays on the server; results
use Klipy's strictest content filter, no customer_id is sent, adverts are
dropped, and answers are cached for ten minutes against the hourly quota.

A GIF is sent as a message of its own carrying Klipy's address (gifOk()
in the rules holds both addresses to klipy.com) and counts as a file for
a room's files policy. Favorites, recents and folders now hold stickers
and GIFs together (g:<slug>), with each saved GIF's details kept on the
library so the picker can draw them without asking Klipy.

Rules change in firestore.rules: not live until scripts/deploy-rules.js
runs. GIF search stays off until KLIPY_API_KEY is set.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add WhatsApp-style stickers to chat, with personal favorites and folders
changes.body:
A sticker button beside the emoji picker opens the company sticker set.
Anyone can add one (resized to 512px WebP in the browser; GIFs kept as
they are, 2 MB cap); whoever added it, or chat.stickers.manage (admin),
can take it off the set. Picking one sends it as a message of its own.

Each person keeps favorites and their own folders in chatLibraries/{uid},
reachable from the picker and by clicking a sticker in a conversation.
Items are prefixed (s:<id>) so GIFs can share the lists later.

A message carries its own copy of the sticker and the file is never
deleted, so removing a sticker from the set does not unsend it. Stickers
count as files for a room's files policy.

Rules change in firestore.rules and storage.rules: not live until
scripts/deploy-rules.js runs.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Open the full emoji set in chat reactions and the message box
changes.body:
The six quick reactions stay first; a + at the end of that row opens a
searchable picker with every emoji, and a smiley beside the paperclip
inserts emoji at the caret. Reaction keys stay ASCII: any emoji outside
the quick six is stored as its code points (u1f525), so no rules change.

The list is a trimmed copy of emojibase-data, built by
scripts/build-emoji-data.js and loaded only when a picker opens. The
picker hides emoji this machine's font cannot draw.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let finance recheck a lane's mileage with Google
changes.body:
The refresh route and the order page's "Recheck with Google" button now
accept laneDistance.manage beside settings.manage, so finance can recheck
the mileage they bill and pay against. The permission's description says
each recheck is charged.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let dispatch manage lead sources and finance manage lane distance and payment terms
changes.body:
Three narrow permissions carved out of settings.manage: leadSources.manage
(dispatch), laneDistance.manage and paymentTerms.manage (finance). The
broad permission still reaches all three, so nobody granted it by hand
loses anything. requirePermission now accepts a list meaning any one of
them. The Operations tab opens to each holder with only their panels on
it, and the People tab stays hidden from them.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Show the carrier's main contact on orders; give carrier contacts a title
changes.body:
Rearranges the order's Carrier section into rows of three: carrier, MC,
DOT; main contact, phone, email; driver, phone, licence; then insurance.
Adds an optional contactTitle to carriers (Dispatcher, Owner, Manager...)
picked from a fixed list on the carrier forms. A carrier with no main
contact falls back to its dispatcher block.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Adapt BATS's Price and Terms block onto orders
changes.body:
Orders get a Price and Terms section in place of Financials: client
payment method, carrier pay terms and broker fee terms (each an
admin-kept list in Settings -> Operations -> Payment Terms, with a fee
and a default payer), special terms, and BATS's complex payment terms
with remaining carrier pay and broker fee. The header shows total
mileage and price per mile.

Each order keeps a copy of the options it was booked with, so changing
a fee in Settings does not rewrite existing loads. The lists live on
appSettings/general, so no rules or index changes.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Add a declared value to each commodity line on orders
changes.body:
Each freight line carries its own value in USD, for all its pieces. The
order stores the sum as commodityValue, derived on save like pieces and
weight. Blank stays null rather than $0, so existing orders read as "not
entered". The order page shows a Value column and a total for multi-line
loads.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Show each party's contact person on orders; label pick-up and delivery
changes.body:
The client, shipper and consignee now show their contact person above
the phone and email - in the order pickers and on the order page. Only
when the party has a company name, since otherwise the contact already
is the displayed name.

On the order page, Shipper and Consignee read "Shipper (Pick-Up
Location)" and "Consignee (Delivery Location)".

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Show carrier MC, DOT and insurance on orders; store MC/DOT as digits
changes.body:
The Carrier section of an order - on the new-order form, when assigning
a carrier, and on the order page - now shows the carrier's MC and DOT,
its certificate of insurance, the insurance expiry and a new coverage
amount. All of it lives on the carrier record, so what is filled in on
one load is what every load with that carrier shows. MC and DOT are
shown as text once on record and only offered as boxes while blank.

Carriers gain insuranceCoverage (whole USD), asked for on both
add-carrier forms and editable on the carrier page.

MC and DOT are now stored as digits only (carrierNumber), applied in
createCarrier/updateCarrier and both BATS importers, because the number
search is an exact match and "MC-123456" could never be found by
123456. Search also accepts a number typed with its prefix.
scripts/backfill-carrier-numbers.js normalizes existing carriers; not
yet run (dry run: one carrier to change).

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Show party phone and email on orders, and put shipper/consignee in Route
changes.body:
The client, shipper and consignee now show their phone and email under
their name - in the picker on the new and edit forms once a record is
linked, and on the order page. Read live from the party record rather
than copied onto the order, and through the same ownership check as the
party page, so seeing a load does not by itself reveal its client's
contact details.

Shipper and consignee move to the Route section, each above the address
it prefills.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Show the ZIP after a linked party's name in the order pickers
changes.body:
Display only: the order still stores the bare name, so its paperwork
is unchanged. Shipper and consignee fall back to their default pickup
or delivery ZIP when the record's own address has none.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Give admin and HR a calendar of birthdays, anniversaries and holidays
changes.body:
A Celebrations page behind people.view, the permission that already shows
these dates in Settings → People. It shows the age somebody is turning and
their years with the company, marks people who opted out of the Everyone-room
post, and lays Guatemala and US public holidays over the month, computed from
their rules rather than stored.

Reminders, per person: a standing rule for every birthday and every
anniversary (on the day, a day before, a week before) and one-offs set from
the calendar. Sent at 8:05am Guatemala by a second Vercel cron, as one email
and one message in a new `notice` chat room that only TTMS can write in —
locked with the existing admins-only policy, so no rules deploy. The run
re-checks people.view at send time.

Also fixes completedYears() for 29 February starters, which made the
Everyone-room post and the dashboard banner say one year too few on the 28th
in non-leap years, and moves the cron secret check into src/lib/cronAuth.ts
so both crons share it.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Show the birthday and anniversary banners on the profile page too
changes.body:
The profile page already loads the caller's own record, so it hands that
to the banner rather than letting it fetch /api/me a second time. The
dashboard still fetches on its own. Closing a banner is remembered per
day in the browser, so closing it on one page closes it on both.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Greet people on their own work anniversary too
changes.body:
The dashboard banner now covers work anniversaries as well as birthdays,
signed the same way and seen only by the person it is about. It follows
the room post's rules: nothing on a first day, "1 year" not "1 years",
and a leap-day date lands on the 28th.

A birthday and an anniversary on the same day show as two banners, each
closed on its own, so dismissing one does not swallow the other. The
component is renamed CelebrationBanner now that it is not only birthdays.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Sign the birthday note at the foot, and greet people on their own dashboard
changes.body:
The company's name used to head the Everyone-room post as an uppercase
label, which read like a notice rather than a greeting. It now signs off
at the bottom, beside the time. Posts already sent change with it, since
the name is drawn from senderName at render time.

The default anniversary line drops "at {company}", which would otherwise
name the company twice now that the post is signed with it.

A birthday banner now sits at the top of the dashboard on your own
birthday, signed the same way. It reads your own date through /api/me,
so nobody else learns anything, and for that reason it ignores the
announceBirthday switch. Closing it is remembered for the day in that
browser.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Sign the birthday note from the company, and let HR write it
changes.body:
The daily post is signed "Total Transport Logistics" rather than TTMS: the
company is speaking, not the software it runs on. That needed a second shape
of system message, not just a different string — the alert shape is an 11px
pill with truncate on it, which cut a greeting off mid-name. An announcement
is drawn as a card with the sender written out and the full text, and stays
inert like an alert: happy birthday belongs to colleagues, and the post is
there to prompt it rather than stand in for it.

The wording belongs to HR now rather than to the code. Two templates in
Settings, gated on a new celebrations.manage that admin and HR hold. Their
shapes differ deliberately: one birthday line for everybody, because two
birthdays differ only in the name, and one anniversary line per person,
because the years do not. An unrecognised placeholder is refused rather than
printed — {Name} for {name} would otherwise go out to the whole company
reading exactly like that — and it is checked in the editor, in the route,
and again when the message is built, because a template edited by hand in the
Console has been through neither of the first two.

celebrations.manage is the first permission to open a Settings tab to a
non-admin, so the Operations page filters its own panels. Drawing a control
whose save will 403 is worse than hiding it.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Put everything a conversation has been sent in one place
changes.body:
Finding a rate sheet somebody attached three weeks ago meant scrolling a
room until it appeared, and the scroll is paged. Search does not help: it
matches file names, and nobody remembers what a scan was called.

Every conversation — a direct thread, a room, a load room — now has a
paperclip in its header, and Room settings has a row pointing at the same
panel. Three tabs, because the three are looked for differently: photos as
a grid, because a photo is recognised by seeing it; documents as rows,
because a document is recognised by its name; links with the sentence they
were pasted in, because that is what somebody remembers a month later.
Every row is a way back to the message it came from.

Firestore can ask neither whether attachments is non-empty nor whether a
string holds a link, so contentKinds is worked out on save — the same trick
searchTerms uses. It rides along with the text everywhere it can move: an
edit rebuilds it, a take-back empties it, so a photo somebody removed stops
being listed. It is a coarse filter and not the answer; the rows are read
off the documents that come back.

Not live until deployed: two composite indexes (contentKinds + createdAt,
on messages and replies), the rules change that lets an edit and a delete
write the field, and scripts/backfill-chat-content-kinds.js for the history
written before it existed.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Say happy birthday, once, at eight in the morning
changes.body:
TTMS posts one line in the Everyone room on the days somebody has a
birthday or a work anniversary — a Vercel cron at 14:00 UTC, which is 8am
in Guatemala all year round.

The dates behind it are payroll fields that admin and HR alone can see, so
the post carries a name and nothing else: no date, no year, no age. An
anniversary adds the number of years, which is the point of saying it.
Anybody can take themselves out of either kind from their own profile.

The run is claimed by creating celebrationRuns/{YYYY-MM-DD}, because Vercel
invokes a cron at least once rather than exactly once, and nobody should be
congratulated twice.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let a removal be undone, and keep the face on the record
changes.body:
Removing someone was final. The entry, the profile and the photo all
went, and putting a mistaken removal right meant retyping a person's
name, phones, birthday, start date, site, team, roles and individual
permissions out of the archive by hand — with the photo gone for good.

Three changes, and they lean on each other:

The photo is no longer deleted. The archive row points at it, so the
removal log shows a face instead of an initial and a restore puts the
photo back with the person. Nothing new is exposed: `avatars/` has
always been readable by every allowlisted account, and the log is
admin-only. Rows archived before today keep falling back to the
initial, because those files are genuinely gone.

Put back rebuilds the allowlist entry from the archived row, through
`POST /api/admin/users/restore` under `people.manage` — the same
authority removal takes. Addressed by the removal id, never the email:
the same address can have been removed twice with different roles, and
the row the admin is looking at is the one they mean. Three deliberate
differences from what was archived — `uid: null`, because the profile
was deleted with the account and an entry naming a uid with no
permissions behind it is a state nothing else here produces; never
restored suspended; and a site or team deleted meanwhile is dropped
rather than left dangling. The archive row is marked, never deleted,
so the log still reads "removed on the 3rd, put back on the 5th", and
the same removal cannot be undone twice.

Access History is the other half. `peopleEvents` records every
addition, removal and restore in order, with the actor and the roles
held at the time — additions included, which the removal log by
definition cannot hold. A failed write never fails the operation, the
opposite of the removal archive: every event already has its own
record elsewhere, and refusing to add somebody because a timeline
write failed is worse than a gap in the timeline.

firestore.rules gains a deny block for `peopleEvents`. It is not live
until `node scripts/deploy-rules.js` runs; nothing breaks meanwhile,
as an undeclared collection is already denied. Both files compile.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Put the chips that do not fit in the menu beside them
changes.body:
The arrows move the row but never say what is along it, so a filter off the
right edge is still something you have to go looking for. The menu on the
chevron now opens with a Not on screen group: every chip the row is not
showing, by name, with its unread count, and picking one selects it and
scrolls its chip back into view.

A chip under an arrow counts as off screen too. The arrows sit over the ends
of the row rather than beside them, so the last chip is usually half under
one, and a click there lands on the arrow — which makes it exactly as
unreachable as a chip past the edge.

The row and the menu now render from one array of chips, so a chip that
scrolls out of reach turns up in the menu under the same name and the same
count it was wearing on the row.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let people reach every filter chip, and size the list themselves
changes.body:
The chip row has scrolled sideways since it was built, but with the scrollbar
hidden a mouse had no way to move it — the only gesture that worked was
pressing a chip and dragging the row, which is not something anybody discovers.
Arrows now fade in over whichever end still has something behind it, and the
wheel scrolls the row instead of the page, handing the wheel back at each end
so a row that has run out does not swallow the scroll of the screen.

The conversation column was fixed at 288px, which is the wrong width twice
over: too narrow for somebody with a dozen lists who wants the chips on one
line, too wide for somebody reading one long thread. The divider between the
list and the thread is now the handle, so being able to choose costs the
layout nothing, and the width stays in this browser — it is about the screen
in front of them, like the chat sound.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let people search what has been said in chat
changes.body:
A search box above the conversation list, doing two different jobs. Typing
narrows the rooms and people the browser already holds, which costs nothing.
Pressing Enter searches every message and reply in every room you are in.

Firestore cannot look inside a string, so each message now stores the words it
can be found by — its text, its sender's name and any file names — worked out
on save, the same trick orderSearchTerms uses. Whole words rather than every
fragment: a 4,000-character message indexed the way an order is would blow the
limit of 40,000 index entries per document.

The search itself runs server-side at GET /api/chat/search. It spans rooms,
which as a client query would be a collection-group query over messages — and
a collection-group rule cannot tell which conversation a document belongs to,
so no rule could gate one. The route resolves the caller's rooms from their own
uid and takes nothing about scope from the request.

Opening a result jumps to the message where it was said, widening the room's
existing window to reach it rather than building a second static view of the
room beside the live one. One aggregation read says how far back it sits;
JUMP_LIMIT is the budget for the messages themselves, and past it the room
opens where it normally would and says so.

Deleting a message empties its words with its text, so a message somebody took
back cannot be read out of a search result.

Already applied to the live project: the rules are deployed, both indexes are
created, and scripts/backfill-chat-search-terms.js has filled in the 76
messages and replies written before this existed.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let people sort their own chats into filter groups
changes.body:
A row of chips above the conversation list: All, Favorites, Unread, Rooms
and Loads, then whatever lists somebody makes for themselves. Favorites is
precreated and cannot be renamed or deleted; the rest of the lists are made,
named and filled from the menu on a chat.

All of it is a filter over conversations the browser already holds, so no
chip is a query and none of this costs a Firestore read. It rides on the
chatReads listener that was already running, and needs no rules change:
that document is already the one thing a person may write about themselves.

Lists are a map keyed by list id rather than an array, so filing one chat
writes lists.<id>.conversationIds alone and two tabs cannot overwrite each
other. Favorites is its own field: it is always there and has no name or
creation date to store.

Every chip carries how many chats under it are unread, because a filter
hides rooms and a hidden room with something waiting in it is the failure
this could have. The conversation being read stays in the column whatever
the filter says — opening one marks it read, so under Unread its own row
would otherwise slide out from under the cursor.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let people put their pinned rooms and threads in their own order
changes.body:
Pinning appended to the list and that was the order for good, so the room
that mattered most was wherever it happened to be pinned.

A pinned row now drags onto another pinned row and takes its place, and
the same move is in the room's menu and on a pinned thread row for anyone
not using a mouse. Only pinned rows take part: the rest of both lists is
sorted by activity and has nowhere for a dropped row to stay.

The order is written whole, which is the one exception to the arrayUnion
rule the pin toggles follow — there is no arrayUnion for "these, in this
order". Both lists share one helper for the maths and one hook for the
drag, so the arrows and the drag cannot drift.

No rules change: chatReads is already the document its owner writes.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let a room be run by the people in it, and say who those are
changes.body:
A named room had no owner. Anybody in it could rename it, change who else was
in it, and pin whatever they liked, on the reasoning that a working room has
no admin to appeal to. That holds until somebody needs one -- a notices room
everybody can talk over, a load rate pasted into the wrong room by the one
person who can take it back.

So a room names its adminUids and carries a policy of six switches -- post,
membership, details, files, links, pins -- each everyone or admins. Every key
is optional and an absent one means everyone, which is what let this land on
live rooms with no backfill and no deploy order to get right. A room made
before admins existed has no list at all and falls back to its createdBy; the
route normalises that on the first save.

Where each switch is enforced is not interchangeable. post, files, links and
pins are in firestore.rules, because messages are written to Firestore
straight from the browser and a check that lived only in the composer would
be a suggestion. membership and details are in the route, which is already
the only thing allowed to write either. The composer asks the same questions
first so a refusal is a sentence rather than "Missing or insufficient
permissions".

Two invariants the rules lean on are kept by the route rather than hoped for:
adminUids never names somebody outside the room, so an empty list means
nobody is left running it; and it is never empty while the room has members
-- the last admin cannot leave without naming a successor, and DELETE answers
409 with the candidates rather than a refusal. The empty case is still
handled, because an account deleted in Settings -> People never passes
through that route.

A mute always has a deadline. There is no forever, the server refuses a
missing or past one, and the expiry is applied where the mute is read rather
than by anything scheduled -- nothing here runs on a schedule, and a mute
that outlived its clock because a job did not fire is the worst failure this
could have. Same shape and same reason as isGrantLive() on an order grant.
The muted person is told in their own composer, with the date; the room is
not. Saying "Vivian muted Tom until Friday" in front of eleven colleagues is
a larger and different act than stopping Tom writing for a day.

A room admin can take a colleague's message back, and only back: the rules
let text go to empty down that branch and nowhere else, so it never becomes a
way to rewrite what somebody said. The tombstone reads "Removed by Vivian",
because a bare "Message deleted" leaves its author assuming they did it.

The Everyone room has no membership array to name admins in, so its one
switch is decided by a new chat.announce permission -- admin and HR by
default, grantable one person at a time. It widens isHr. Left set to everyone
so the deploy does not silently stop the company posting; the gear is in the
room header for anybody holding it.

Who is in it now lists the room's members, admins first, with an admin
toggle, a mute and a remove on each, and adds people through a search box.
The grid of every account in the company with ticks beside them made the
question people open that panel to ask -- who is in this room -- something
you had to work out by scanning forty rows.

Permission changes write a memberEvents entry beside the membership ones and
post one line in the room, so somebody whose composer has gone grey can find
out who turned it off and when.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let a chat message draw a card for a load somebody linked
changes.body:
An order card already appeared under any message saying TTL26000042 or
#41207, but not under the link people actually produce -- the address bar
copied out of the order they were already looking at.

A link carries a document id where the other shapes carry a number, so the
matcher returns refs rather than strings and /api/orders/lookup takes ?id=
alongside ?number=. Both are checked the same way, through canSeeOrder() and
the same standing grants: a link is not a way to see a load you could not
open by walking to it. A 403 still draws nothing and leaves the link as the
plain text it was typed as.

The hosts a link must be on are a fixed list, not APP_URL -- that constant is
localhost on every staff machine -- and not window.location, which differs
between the server render and the browser one. Matching the path alone would
sprout one of our cards under any site with a page at the same address.

Cards are now loaded together and deduplicated by order id, so a load named
by number and linked in the same breath draws one card instead of two.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let the dashboard raise an alert again, for every load a person owns
changes.body:
The Needs Attention panel had rendered nothing for anybody since abd99dc,
which moved it off a full read of the order book and onto the samples the
dashboard summary already returns. Those come over JSON from
/api/orders/summary, where a Timestamp arrives as `{_seconds, _nanoseconds}`
with no methods on it, and alerts.ts tested `typeof ts.toDate === 'function'`
before reading a date. Every rule is gated on a date, so every rule was
skipped, getAlerts returned an empty list, and AlertPanel renders null on an
empty list — the section did not break, it disappeared.

Read the dates through toDate() in dateFormat.ts instead, which has known
about that shape since the same trap emptied every date on the screen.

The same move left three fields out of the summary's projection, so three
rules could not have fired even with the dates working: deliveryDate for a
late load, invoiceStoragePath for an uninvoiced one, createdAt for a stale
quote. A projection reads the same whatever it names, and this is a sample
of at most twenty-five documents per card, so they go back in.

Alerts are no longer filtered by createdBy either. The samples arrive
already narrowed — an admin sees the book, everybody else comes through
summariseInMemory() and listVisibleOrdersPage(), which is the union of
assigned-to-them, their groups' and their clients' loads. Filtering on top
of that dropped a load the moment it was assigned to somebody rather than
raised by them, which is most of them.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let a room say who was added to it and who left
changes.body:
Changing who is in a chat room left no trace at all: any member could add
or remove anybody else, and a month later there was nothing to say who had
done it or that it had happened.

Each change now writes an entry to conversations/{id}/memberEvents -- the
same shape and the same argument as ownerEvents on an order -- and posts a
line into the room, drawn as the centred line an order alert already uses.
Room settings reads the entries back as a History section.

The membership, its entry and its line go in one batch, so a change cannot
save without the record of it. Group rooms only: a direct thread cannot
change members, the company room has none, and a record room is joined by
whoever opens the load, so a row per reader would record who had looked at
an order rather than who was let in.

systemLine() is pulled out of postOrderAlert for the second caller, and
hands its conversation bump back rather than writing it -- one commit may
not write the same document twice, and both callers are already updating
the room.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let a name pair stay on one line when its label is long
changes.body:
The label was glued to the left-hand box as "{label} — First Name",
which sat level with a bare "Last Name" only while the label was one
short word. "Contact (optional)" wraps to two lines and takes its own
input down a row with it, so the two boxes ended up on different levels
on the shipper and consignee forms.

The label now heads the pair, with First Name and Last Name as their own
lighter labels beneath it. Every name pair in the app moves together —
carrier contact, dispatcher, billing contact, driver, quick-add carrier —
rather than one screen getting a layout of its own.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let a dock be saved without a name and an inbox it does not have
changes.body:
The contact name and email are no longer required when the record being
created is a shipper or a consignee. A broker booking a load usually has
the facility's address and a number for the gate and nothing else, and
nothing we send leaves for either of them — the load confirmation goes to
the client, the rate confirmation to the carrier. Requiring both anyway
meant a made-up name typed in to get past the form, which is worse on the
record than an empty box.

A client is still held to both, so a record ticked as a client as well as
a dock stays strict. Company name, phone and address stay required on all
three. Anything that is filled in is still checked.

The line under both headings is now one exported partyRequirementNote
rather than the same sentence pasted on two screens, so the copy cannot
promise something validatePartyDraft does not enforce.

changes.author: erwindank
changes.subject: Let a phone number say which country it is in
changes.body:
Client, shipper, consignee, carrier and driver numbers - and the driver
number copied onto a load - now carry the country beside them: US, Mexico,
Canada or Guatemala, picked from a dropdown that starts on US.

The country is picked, never guessed, and that is structural rather than
lazy. Mexican and US numbers are both ten digits and Canada shares the US
country code outright, so nothing in the digits could tell the three apart.
src/lib/phone.ts already made that call for staff numbers and says so at
length; this is the same decision for the records.

Three parts:

- PhoneField is the one way a number is typed now, the way DateField is for
  dates. It tidies on blur - a number that reads as the chosen country is
  rewritten into the house format - and it never blanks one that does not,
  which is where it parts company with the staff spreadsheet importer. A
  form somebody is watching must not empty a field in front of them.

- US and Canada are written +1 (469) 935-4100. They were +(469) 935-4100,
  a + followed by an area code with no country code after it - it read as
  though 469 were a country, and could not be dialled as printed from
  Monterrey. Now the rule is the same for all four: the + is always
  followed by the country code.

- The party phone lookup no longer assumes a US-length number. toPhoneKey
  kept the last ten digits, so a Guatemalan number stored with its country
  code was filed under a key that starts inside the 502, and the person who
  dials it locally every week would never find it - silently. A number is
  now filed under its national form and its international one, and a search
  offers every reading of what was typed through array-contains-any. The
  legacy last-ten key is still stored, so re-keying can only add matches,
  never remove one, and nothing findable today stops being findable.

Nothing here needs a migration to be correct: phoneRegionOf() answers US
for a record with no region, which is what every existing record relies on.
Three optional passes tidy up behind it, each dry-runnable and none yet run:

  scripts/backfill-phone-regions.js    stamps US on 22 existing records
  scripts/restyle-phone-numbers.js     rewrites 51 numbers into the new
                                       format, staff numbers included
